import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.HardyLittlewood

/-!
# Erdős Problem 855

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)

This is an "eventually" formulation of the Second Hardy–Littlewood conjecture.
-/

open Filter
open scoped Nat.Prime

namespace Erdos855

/--
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for sufficiently large $x, y$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_855 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∀ᶠ y in atTop, π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y := by
  sorry

end Erdos855

findings.description: The nested eventual quantifiers on line 38 expand to `∃ X, ∀ x ≥ X, ∃ Y, ∀ y ≥ Y, π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y`, so the cutoff Y may depend on x. The source's assertion for sufficiently large x and y requires a uniform cutoff: `∃ N, ∀ x y, N ≤ x → N ≤ y → π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y`. The formalization permits exceptional pairs with both coordinates arbitrarily large, provided each fixed sufficiently large x has only finitely many exceptional y. It therefore omits the required uniformity.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/855, also available verbatim at https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/855: “If π(x) counts the number of primes in [1,x] then is it true that (for large x and y) π(x+y) ≤ π(x)+π(y)?” The referenced Hardy–Littlewood conjecture is stated for all integers x,y ≥ 2 in Richards, “On the Incompatibility of Two Conjectures Concerning Primes” (1974), pp. 420–422; the Erdős Problems page relaxes this to sufficiently large pairs, not an x-dependent cutoff for y.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the right-hand side by `∀ᶠ p : ℕ × ℕ in atTop, π (p.1 + p.2) ≤ π p.1 + π p.2`. Equivalently, use `∃ N : ℕ, ∀ x y : ℕ, N ≤ x → N ≤ y → π (x + y) ≤ π x + π y`. Keep the outer `answer(sorry) ↔`.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved (1985), §6, pp. 80–82: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf
P. Erdős, Some unsolved problems (1961), Problem I.1, pp. 221–222: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1961-22.pdf
I. Richards, On the Incompatibility of Two Conjectures Concerning Primes (1974), especially §1.1: https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1974-80-03/S0002-9904-1974-13434-8/S0002-9904-1974-13434-8.pdf
review.notes: The source still marks the problem OPEN; its conditional incompatibility with the prime-tuples conjecture is not an unconditional resolution. Erdős pages and the primary-paper PDFs were read through r.jina.ai. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, Lean verified both quantifier expansions, the uniform-to-iterated implication, and a symmetric predicate separating the filters (`x ≠ y`); that separation is not a counterexample about primes. Confirmed that π counts primes up to and including its natural-number argument, tested small inputs, and proved that explicitly imposing x,y ≥ 2 does not change the eventual predicate. No other mathematical defects found in the file's sole declaration.

submission.summary: Replaced the nested eventual quantifiers with a single eventual quantifier over ℕ × ℕ, requiring a uniform cutoff for both variables. Preserved the answer slot, docstrings, references, and attributes. The requested compile command succeeds with only the permitted `declaration uses sorry` warning.
